readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: Being invited to a paid workplace trial versus being expected to learn off the clock. This article is explicitly about work, not a claim about personal AI use.
readerContract.surfaceJob: Correct the existing dated Front PAiGE article without turning a representation gap into blame or an unsupported causal finding.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: I can recognize an opportunity gap and ask who has control over the conditions.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: The reports show women receiving a smaller share of AI hires and leadership roles, and a separate difference in daily workplace AI use. They do not establish individual ability or causes.
causalSequence: Distinguish hiring, leadership and frequency populations.
Outcome measures cannot identify why a particular person uses a tool less often.
A hypothetical trial makes employer-controlled permission, paid time and selection visible.
Readers can ask about access; managers can change selection and support. Neither guarantees career advancement.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: Imagine two equally interested colleagues: one receives an approved tool and paid trial time; the other does not. Their usage cannot be treated as a fair enthusiasm comparison.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A manager invites only existing users to a new trial; ask how newcomers can get supported access rather than assume the invitation is equally accessible.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Ask how to join an approved trial and what paid learning time is available; managers publish invitations and selection criteria.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means; Cocktail; Watch Fors; Closing; Class Notes.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Lead with the evidence; no historical capability hook or obligatory nostalgia analogy.
